arxiv-2004-01168.title: Evaluating the Calibration of Knowledge Graph Embeddings for Trustworthy Link Prediction
arxiv-2004-01168.creator: Tara Safavi, Danai Koutra, Edgar Meij
arxiv-2004-01168.description: Abstract Little is known about the trustworthiness of predictions made by knowledge graph embedding (KGE) models. In this paper we take initial steps toward this direction by investigating the calibration of KGE models, or the extent to which they output confidence scores that reflect the expected correctness of predicted knowledge graph triples.

arxiv-2109-02550.title: You should evaluate your language model on marginal likelihood over tokenisations
arxiv-2109-02550.creator: Kris Cao, Laura Rimell
arxiv-2109-02550.description: Abstract Neural language models typically tokenise input text into sub-word units to achieve an open vocabulary. The standard approach is to use a single canonical tokenisation at both train and test time. We suggest that this approach is unsatisfactory and may bottleneck our evaluation of language model performance.

arxiv-2112-09137.title: Cosmological constraints on the decay of heavy relics into neutrinos
arxiv-2112-09137.creator: and Matteo Lucca
arxiv-2112-09137.description: Abstract A massive particle decaying into neutrinos in the early Universe is known to be less constrained than if it was decaying into other standard model particles. However, even if the decay proceeds into neutrinos, the latter still inevitably emit secondary particles undergoing electromagnetic interactions that can be probed.

arxiv-2204-09395.title: Adjusting Thermal Stability in Double-Barrier MTJ for Energy Improvement in Cryogenic STT-MRAMs
arxiv-2204-09395.creator: Esteban Garzón, Raffaele De Rose, Felice Crupi, Lionel Trojman, Adam Teman, Marco Lanuzza
arxiv-2204-09395.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Esteban Garzón, Raffaele De Rose, Felice Crupi, Lionel Trojman, Adam Teman, Marco Lanuzza. This paper investigates the impact of thermal stability relaxation in double-barrier magnetic tunnel junctions (DMTJs) for energy-efficient spin-transfer torque magnetic random access memories (STT-MRAMs) operating at the liquid nitrogen boiling point (77 K \mathrm{K} ). Our study is carried out through a macrospin-based Verilog-A compact model of DMTJ, along with a 65 nm \mathrm{nm} commercial process design kit (PDK) calibrated down to 77 K \mathrm{K} under silicon measurements.

arxiv-2301-09496.title: ECGAN: Self-supervised generative adversarial network for electrocardiography
arxiv-2301-09496.creator: Lorenzo Simone, Davide Bacciu
arxiv-2301-09496.description: Abstract High-quality synthetic data can support the development of effective predictive models for biomedical tasks, especially in rare diseases or when subject to compelling privacy constraints. These limitations, for instance, negatively impact open access to electrocardiography datasets about arrhythmias. This work introduces a self-supervised approach to the generation of synthetic electrocardiography time series which is shown to promote morphological plausibility.

arxiv-2308-08591.title: A massive helium star with a sufficiently strong magnetic field to form a magnetar
arxiv-2308-08591.creator: Tomer Shenar, Gregg A. Wade, Pablo Marchant, Stefano Bagnulo, Julia Bodensteiner, Dominic M. Bowman, Avishai Gilkis, Norbert Langer, André Nicolas-Chené, Lidia Oskinova, Timothy Van Reeth, Hugues Sana, Nicole St-Louis, Alexandre Soares de Oliveira, Helge Todt, Silvia Toonen
arxiv-2308-08591.description: Abstract Magnetars are highly magnetized neutron stars; their formation mechanism is unknown. Hot helium-rich stars with spectra dominated by emission lines are known as Wolf-Rayet stars. We observe the binary system HD 45166 using spectropolarimetry, finding that it contains a Wolf-Rayet star with a mass of 2 solar masses and a magnetic field of 43 kilogauss.

arxiv-2402-14069.title: New Mass Window for Primordial Black Holes as Dark Matter from Memory Burden Effect
arxiv-2402-14069.creator: Ana Alexandre, Gia Dvali, Emmanouil Koutsangelas
arxiv-2402-14069.description: Abstract The mass ranges allowed for Primordial Black Holes (PBHs) to constitute all of Dark Matter (DM) are broadly constrained. However, these constraints rely on the standard semiclassical approximation which assumes that the evaporation process is self-similar. Quantum effects such as memory burden take the evaporation process out of the semiclassical regime latest by half-decay time.

arxiv-2404-05638.title: Holographic supersymmetric Rényi entropies from hyperbolic black holes with scalar hair
arxiv-2404-05638.creator: Jie Ren, and Dao-Quan Sun
arxiv-2404-05638.description: Abstract We study holographic supersymmetric Rényi entropies from a family of hyperbolic black holes in an Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton (EMD) system under the BPS condition. We calculate the thermodynamic quantities of these hyperbolic black holes. We find a remarkably simple formula of the supersymmetric Rényi entropy that unifies (interpolates) 11 cases embeddable to 10 or 11 dimensional supergravity.

arxiv-2405-05143.title: Learning Object Semantic Similarity with Self-Supervision 1 Shared first authorship, 2 shared last authorship.
arxiv-2405-05143.creator: Arthur Aubret 1,2, 1 , Timothy Schaumlöffel 3,4, 1 , Gemma Roig 3,4, 2 , Jochen Triesch 1,3, 2
arxiv-2405-05143.description: Abstract Humans judge the similarity of two objects not just based on their visual appearance but also based on their semantic relatedness. However, it remains unclear how humans learn about semantic relationships between objects and categories. One important source of semantic knowledge is that semantically related objects frequently co-occur in the same context.

arxiv-2408-06015.title: Subgraphs with a positive minimum semidegree in digraphs with large outdegree
arxiv-2408-06015.creator: Andrzej Grzesik, Vojtěch Rödl, Jan Volec
arxiv-2408-06015.description: Abstract We prove that every n n -vertex directed graph G G with the minimum outdegree δ + ​ ( G ) = d \delta^{+}(G)=d contains a subgraph H H satisfying min ⁡ { δ + ​ ( H ) , δ − ​ ( H ) } ≥ d ⁡ ( d + 1 ) 2 ​ n .

arxiv-2408-07287.title: Abductive Reasoning in a Paraconsistent Framework
arxiv-2408-07287.creator: Meghyn Bienvenu, Katsumi Inoue, Daniil Kozhemiachenko
arxiv-2408-07287.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Meghyn Bienvenu, Katsumi Inoue, Daniil Kozhemiachenko. We explore the problem of explaining observations starting from a classically inconsistent theory by adopting a paraconsistent framework. We consider two expansions of the well-known Belnap–Dunn paraconsistent four-valued logic 𝖡𝖣 \mathsf{BD} : 𝖡𝖣 ∘ \mathsf{BD}_{\circ} introduces formulas of the form ∘ ϕ \circ\phi (‘the information about ϕ \phi is reliable’), while 𝖡𝖣 △ \mathsf{BD}_{\triangle} augments the language with formulas △ ​ ϕ \triangle\phi (‘there is information that ϕ \phi is true’).

arxiv-2505-04358.title: Reduced cloud cover errors in a hybrid AI-climate model through equation discovery and automatic tuning
arxiv-2505-04358.creator: Arthur Grundner, Tom Beucler, Julien Savre, Axel Lauer, Manuel Schlund, Veronika Eyring
arxiv-2505-04358.description: Abstract Climate models rely on parameterizations that account for the effects of small-scale processes on large-scale dynamics. Particularly cloud-related parameterizations remain a major source of uncertainty in climate projections. While hybrid Earth system models (ESMs) with machine learning-based parameterizations could improve current ESMs, deep learning approaches often lack interpretability, physical consistency, and computational efficiency.

arxiv-2505-23735.title: Atlas : Learning to Optimally Memorize the Context at Test Time
arxiv-2505-23735.creator: Vahab Mirrokni
arxiv-2505-23735.description: Abstract Transformers have been established as the most popular backbones in sequence modeling, mainly due to their effectiveness in in-context retrieval tasks and the ability to learn at scale. Their quadratic memory and time complexity, however, bound their applicability in longer sequences and so has motivated researchers to explore effective alternative architectures such as modern recurrent neural networks (a.k.

arxiv-2509-24895.title: Towards Understanding the Shape of Representations in Protein Language Models
arxiv-2509-24895.creator: Kosio Beshkov, Anders Malthe-Sørenssen
arxiv-2509-24895.description: Abstract While protein language models (PLMs) are one of the most promising avenues of research for future de novo protein design, the way in which they transform sequences to hidden representations, as well as the information encoded in such representations is yet to be fully understood.

arxiv-2601-00069.title: Diagnosing Critical Behavior in AdS Einstein-Maxwell-Scalar Theory via Holographic Entanglement Measures
arxiv-2601-00069.creator: Zhe Yang 1,2, GuangZai Ye 2, Jian-Pin Wu 1, Peng Liu 2
arxiv-2601-00069.description: Abstract We investigate the holographic mixed-state entanglement measures in the Einstein-Maxwell-Scalar (EMS) theory. Several quantities are computed, including the holographic entanglement entropy (HEE), mutual information (MI), entanglement wedge cross-section (EWCS), and butterfly velocity ( v B v_{B} ). Our findings demonstrate that these measures can effectively diagnose phase transitions.

arxiv-2602-12906.title: Gaps and Rings: A Near-Universal Trait of Extended Protoplanetary Discs
arxiv-2602-12906.creator: Q. Bosschaart, O.M. Guerra-Alvarado, N. van der Marel, G.D. Mulders
arxiv-2602-12906.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Q. Bosschaart, O.M. Guerra-Alvarado, N. van der Marel, G.D. Mulders. Substructures such as rings, gaps, and cavities are commonly observed in protoplanetary discs and are thought to play a key role in dust evolution and planet formation. However, a fraction of the extended discs (68% dust radii >30 AU) in nearby star-forming regions remain unresolved, leaving their substructure content uncertain and thereby limiting our understanding of dust evolution and the initial conditions for planet formation across the full disc population.

catholic-encyclopedia-1913-aloysius-gent.creator: Louis Charles Casartelli
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-aloysius-gent.description: Article 'Aloysius Gentili' from the Catholic Encyclopedia (1913), the 15-volume English-language reference work published 1907-1914 by Robert Appleton Company.

The toolset integrates many databases, including Gene Ontology, KEGG and TRANSFAC, to provide a comprehensive and in-depth analysis...

europmc-pmc7868676.creator: Bulcha JT, Wang Y, Ma H, Tai PWL, Gao G.
europmc-pmc7868676.description: Throughout its 40-year history, the field of gene therapy has been marked by many transitions. It has seen great strides in combating human disease, has given hope to patients and families with limited treatment options, but has also been subject to many setbacks. Treatment of...

plos-pone-0003940.title: The Pace of Prostatic Intraepithelial Neoplasia Development Is Determined by the Timing of Pten Tumor Suppressor Gene Excision
plos-pone-0003940.creator: H. Artee Luchman, Hallgrimur Benediktsson, Michelle L. Villemaire et al.
plos-pone-0003940.description: PLOS ONE research article. Loss of the PTEN tumor suppressor is a common occurrence in human prostate cancer, particularly in advanced disease. In keeping with its role as a pivotal upstream regulator of the phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase signaling pathway, experimentally-induced deletion of Pten in the mur

pmc-11330982.title: Subject-specific atlas for automatic brain tissue segmentation of neonatal magnetic resonance images
pmc-11330982.creator: Negar Noorizadeh, Kamran Kazemi, Seyedeh Masoumeh Taji, Habibollah Danyali, Ardalan Aarabi
pmc-11330982.description: Developing advanced systems for 3D brain tissue segmentation from neonatal magnetic resonance (MR) images is vital for newborn structural analysis. However, automatic segmentation of neonatal brain tissues is challenging due to smaller head size and inverted T1/T2 tissue contrast compared to adults.

pmc-11345177.title: Model-driven engineering for digital twins: a graph model-based patient simulation application
pmc-11345177.creator: William Trevena, Xiang Zhong, Amos Lal, Lucrezia Rovati, Edin Cubro, Yue Dong, Phillip Schulte, Ognjen Gajic
pmc-11345177.description: IntroductionDigital twins of patients are virtual models that can create a digital patient replica to test clinical interventions in silico without exposing real patients to risk. With the increasing availability of electronic health records and sensor-derived patient data, digital twins offer significant potential for applications in the healthcare sector.

pmc-11389223.title: Effectiveness of a home-based, post-discharge early intervention program for very preterm infants in reducing parental stress: a randomized controlled trial
pmc-11389223.creator: Juan Fan, Ruiyun He, Shasha He, Mei Yang, Xiaojun Tao, Mei Zhou, Xiong Gao, Weihong Yu, Jianhui Wang
pmc-11389223.description: BackgroundThis study aims to evaluate the impact of a home-based, post-discharge early intervention (EI) program on reducing parental stress levels in families with preterm infants born between 28+ 0 and 31+ 6 weeks gestational age.MethodsA randomized controlled trial was conducted, with families randomly allocated to either the EI or standard care (SC) group.

pmc-12786676.title: High-Resolution 1H NMR Investigation of the Speciation Status of Nickel(II) and Copper(II) Ions in a Cell Culture Medium: Relevance to Their Toxicological Actions
pmc-12786676.creator: Deepinder K. Kalra, Kayleigh Hunwin, Katie Hewitt, Olivia Steel, Martin Grootveld
pmc-12786676.description: Copper and nickel ions play pivotal, albeit distinct, roles as essential trace elements in living systems, and primarily serve as co-factors for a range of enzymes. However, as with all trace metal ions, excessive concentrations can exert adverse toxicological properties.

pmc-13178713.title: Retinal Microvascular Disease in Diabetes and Its Prognostic Utility for Cardiovascular and Renal Complications: A Comprehensive Literature Review
pmc-13178713.creator: Jhon Alexander Ponce Alencastro, Génesis María Dommar Alcalá, Ximena Sofía Solares Ovando, Rafael Eduardo Escandón González, Carolina Cristina García Garrote, Haizel Valencia Romero, Valeria de Jesús Meléndez González
pmc-13178713.description: Retinal microvascular impairments are recognized as a non-invasive measure of systemic vascular injury in patients with diabetes. Change in retinal structure and function may serve as markers of renal and cardiovascular microvascular pathology, thereby providing a potential source of prognostic information for predicting outcomes of diabetic kidney disease (DKD), chronic kidney disease (CKD), and cardiovascular disease (CVD).

pmc-13408472.title: A hybrid KF–GAIN framework for dynamic state estimation in islanded microgrids under missing PMU data and line impedance uncertainty
pmc-13408472.creator: Mohammad Reza Masoudi, Mohammad Mohammadi, Behrooz Zaker, Dariush Keihan Asl, Majid Mostafanezhad
pmc-13408472.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The similar time constants of voltage source inverter-based distributed generation units and other components in islanded microgrids (IMGs) pose significant challenges for dynamic state estimation (DSE). To address these issues, particularly under conditions of missing measurement data and uncertainties in line impedances, this paper proposes a linear hybrid framework that combines the Kalman Filter (KF) with a deep learning model called the generative adversarial imputation network (GAIN) for DSE in IMGs.

pmc-13531417.title: Synthesis, X-ray structures and biological evaluation of novel α-aminophosphonate derivatives as anti-inflammatory and antioxidant agents: an integrated in vitro and in silico study
pmc-13531417.creator: Zoubir Douib, Hacene K’tir, Haiet Douib, Zinelaabidine Cheraiet, Taha Khaldi, Latifa Khattabi, Brahim Harkati, Vincent Dorcet, Fabrice Pointillart
pmc-13531417.description: In the field of medicinal chemistry, the design of small molecules is acknowledged as an effective strategy. This study may contribute to the global fight against inflammatory diseases by focusing on the synthesis of novel α-aminophosphonate derivatives incorporating para-aminobenzoic acid (PABA) and benzocaine moieties and evaluating their anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities.

pmc-13544282.title: Comparison of Long-Term Survival Between Nivolumab Plus Ipilimumab and Nivolumab Plus Ipilimumab With Chemotherapy in Advanced NSCLC: A Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Study
pmc-13544282.creator: Kiyohide Komuta, Kinnosuke Matsumoto, Motohiro Tamiya, Takayuki Shiroyama, Yuhei Kinehara, Akihiro Tamiya, Tomoki Kuge, Junji Uchida, Hidekazu Suzuki, Suguru Yamamoto, Satoshi Tobita, Toshie Niki, Satoshi Tetsumoto, Osamu Morimura, Akio Osa, Toshiyuki Minami, Kazumi Nishino, Yoshito Takeda, Atsushi
pmc-13544282.description: IntroductionPivotal clinical trials have reported the survival benefits of both nivolumab plus ipilimumab (NI) and nivolumab plus ipilimumab with 2 cycles of platinum-based chemotherapy (NICT) compared with chemotherapy. However, real-world evidence comparing NI and NICT with long-term follow-up remains limited.MethodsWe retrospectively analyzed 181 patients treated with NICT or NI across 13 institutions in Japan.

pmc-13625633.title: Brain-binding auto-antibodies in subjects with and without post-COVID-syndrome after SARS-CoV-2 infection
pmc-13625633.creator: Majd Faraj, Karin Weissenborn, Bianca Teegen, Meike Dirks, Ann-Katrin Hennemann, Vanessa Wuttke, Winfried Stöcker, Nina Gödecke, Rainer Blasczyk, Anika Großhennig, Hannelore Ehrenreich, Gernot Beutel
pmc-13625633.description: Various pathomechanisms are discussed as possible causes of Post-COVID syndrome (PCS). Immune system dysfunction with increase of autoimmune responses is one of them. Whether the observed increase of autoantibody prevalence after COVID-19 is of any significance for the well-being of affected subjects in the long-term is controversial.
